title: Incident report: a report worker that never released its place
summary: Một tác vụ tạo báo cáo bị dừng nhưng vẫn giữ quyền xử lý, khiến các báo cáo sau phải chờ. Nhóm tìm nguyên nhân, khôi phục hàng đợi và đề xuất cơ chế thu hồi quyền có kiểm tra.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: At 8:40 on Tuesday, the support team received three messages about weekly reports that had not arrived. The report page showed each request as waiting, although the customers had submitted them before breakfast. Other parts of the service were working normally, and customers could still open reports from earlier weeks. Minh, the engineer on duty, first checked whether the delay affected every customer or only a particular group. All three messages concerned customers whose reports used the larger reporting queue. The smaller queue was still producing files. This difference helped Minh narrow the investigation without making changes to the whole service.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The larger queue normally allowed one worker to prepare a report at a time. Before starting, that worker recorded its name beside the current request, showing that it owned the work. A later worker was expected to wait until the name disappeared. During the previous night's maintenance, one worker had stopped unexpectedly after recording its name but before producing a file. Its ownership record remained in place. The next worker therefore behaved as designed and waited. The problem was not a shortage of machines: adding another worker would have created another process waiting for the same ownership record to disappear.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Minh considered removing the record immediately, but first needed to establish whether the original worker was still active somewhere. If two workers prepared the same request, customers might receive competing versions of a report. He checked the worker list, its final log entry, and the storage area where completed files appeared. None showed continuing activity from that worker. A colleague checked the same evidence before Minh acted. They also saved a copy of the ownership record, including its time and request number, so that the investigation would not depend on anyone remembering what had been visible before the recovery.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: At 9:25, Minh removed the abandoned ownership record and allowed the next worker to continue. He did not move the waiting requests into a new queue because their original order was useful to both support staff and customers. The oldest waiting report finished first. During recovery, support published a short notice explaining that report preparation was delayed while existing reports remained available. Staff gave customers the time of the next update rather than promising an exact completion time. By 10:10, the queue had returned to its usual length, and support checked that the three customers had received their reports.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The review found that the ownership arrangement relied on a worker always reaching its final cleanup step. That assumption had seemed reasonable when reports were small and workers rarely stopped during preparation. The team proposed a time limit on ownership, supported by a regular activity message from the worker. An expired record would trigger a check before another worker took over. However, a long report could still be healthy even if it took more time than usual. The team therefore rejected a simple rule that would remove every record after ten minutes, regardless of what the worker was actually doing.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Testing would cover both a worker that stopped completely and one that continued slowly. In the slow case, ownership should remain with the active worker while its activity messages arrived. In the stopped case, a replacement should continue only after the checks found no active owner. The team also added a separate test for two workers attempting to claim one request at nearly the same moment. These tests would run with sample reports containing invented customer information. Support asked for a visible warning when a request had waited unusually long, since customers often noticed the delay before engineers examined the queue.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The final action list separated immediate monitoring from the proposed change. Minh would review queue waiting times each morning until the new ownership checks were released. Another engineer would prepare the change, and support would review the wording of the warning. The team decided to introduce the checks to the smaller queue first, where a problem would affect fewer requests and be easier to observe. Success would mean that stopped workers no longer blocked later reports, while slow but active workers could still finish safely. The incident record would remain open until both behaviours had been demonstrated during the trial.

title: Workshop procedure: checking whether a packing instruction works
summary: Một kho hàng thử nghiệm hướng dẫn đóng gói mới với nhân viên có kinh nghiệm khác nhau. Nhóm quan sát cách thực hiện, sửa chỗ khó hiểu và chỉ triển khai khi hướng dẫn hoạt động trong điều kiện thực tế.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The warehouse training team had rewritten the instruction for packing small desk organisers. The old sheet included several photographs, but workers still asked which cardboard piece belonged under the product and which belonged beside it. Supervisors usually answered these questions during a shift, so the confusion had never appeared in a formal training record. When the company planned to employ twelve temporary workers for the busy season, Lan suggested testing the new sheet before printing copies for every packing table. The workshop would examine the instruction itself, rather than judge how quickly individual workers could learn a task from memory.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Lan invited six employees with different levels of experience. Two packed the product regularly, two worked elsewhere in the warehouse, and two had joined the company that month. Each person received the same materials and a numbered copy of the draft instruction. The experienced workers were asked to follow the sheet even when they already knew another method. Otherwise, their knowledge might hide a missing step. Participants worked separately during the first round so that one person's explanation would not influence another person's choices. A trainer remained nearby to stop any unsuitable handling, but ordinary questions were recorded before being answered.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The observers used a simple record with three columns: the step number, what the participant did, and what appeared to cause uncertainty. They avoided writing comments such as careless or slow, because those words did not explain how the instruction could improve. Instead, one observer wrote that a participant turned the box around twice while trying to match it to the photograph. Another recorded a question about whether the paper label should cover the opening. Participants were told that pauses were useful evidence. They could also explain what they expected a sentence or picture to mean after completing the first attempt.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The most useful finding concerned a photograph taken from directly above the box. Three participants placed the side support underneath the product because the picture did not show its folded edge clearly. The written sentence was technically accurate, but it used the phrase narrow support without identifying the piece by its visible shape. Lan replaced that phrase with folded side piece and added a photograph from an angle. The revision required more space on the page, so she removed a decorative heading to keep the text readable. She kept the step numbers unchanged so that the observation notes still matched the draft.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: A second issue appeared near the end of the process. The sheet told workers to close the box before checking whether the small instruction card was inside. Experienced participants noticed the problem and reopened their boxes, while a new employee assumed the card should be attached outside. The team moved the card check before the closing step. They also separated checking the contents from checking the outer label, since the two checks happened at different moments. Lan declined a suggestion to add every possible packing mistake to the sheet. A long warning list might make the normal sequence harder to follow.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The revised sheet was tested the next afternoon with four employees who had not attended the first workshop. This time, everyone placed the folded piece correctly, but one person missed the final label check after an interruption. The observers had deliberately included a short question from a supervisor to make the trial closer to an ordinary shift. In response, the team added a small completion box beside the final check. Workers could mark it after returning to the table. The team did not claim that the instruction could prevent every error; it needed to support people when attention was divided.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Before printing, Lan asked the shift supervisors to confirm that the material names matched the names used on the storage shelves. The approved sheet would carry a revision date and a contact name for reporting unclear steps. During the first week of use, supervisors would collect questions at the end of each shift and send them to training. Old copies would be removed from the tables when the replacement arrived. The team planned another review after the busy season, when it could compare workshop findings with everyday experience. Printing was therefore the beginning of continued observation, rather than the end of the work.

title: Community notice: sharing freezer space during the kitchen renovation
summary: Bếp chung của khu nhà tạm đóng để cải tạo. Thông báo giải thích cách đăng ký chỗ trong tủ đông thay thế, ghi nhãn hộp, xử lý thay đổi và phối hợp khi chuyển đồ về bếp mới.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The shared kitchen at River House will close for renovation from 4 November to 18 November. Residents may continue using their own kitchen equipment, but the large community freezer must be moved out before the contractors begin. A smaller freezer will be available in the ground-floor meeting room during the closure. It cannot hold everything currently stored in the kitchen, so the residents' committee has prepared a temporary booking arrangement. This notice explains how to request space and how the move will work. Please read it before carrying any boxes downstairs, since an empty-looking shelf may already be reserved for another household.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Each household may request one storage basket for the first week. Send your flat number and the approximate size of your containers to the committee by Friday evening. A committee member will reply with a basket number or explain that the request is on the waiting list. A request is confirmed only when you receive a basket number. The committee will not allocate space according to how many people answer the building's group message first. Instead, it will consider whether a household has another freezer available and whether its containers can fit within one basket without occupying a neighbour's space.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before the move, please put a clear household label on every container. The label should show your flat number and a contact name; the committee does not need a description of every meal. Containers must close properly and fit fully inside the allocated basket. Loose plastic bags are difficult to identify when several households use similar bags, so place them inside a labelled container if possible. The committee will provide a few reusable boxes, but these must be requested in advance. Do not leave extra items on top of another basket, even if the freezer appears quiet when you visit.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The main transfer will take place on Sunday between 9:00 and 11:00. Residents should carry their own containers to the meeting room after a volunteer has checked their basket number. Two volunteers will help households that have already requested assistance with carrying. They will not open containers or decide which items a household should keep. If you cannot attend, you may nominate a neighbour to make the transfer for you. Tell the committee that person's name beforehand. Anything left in the old freezer after the transfer period will be recorded, and the household named on its label will be contacted.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The meeting room will remain available for small gatherings, so access to the freezer needs to be predictable. Residents can collect or add containers between 7:00 and 9:00 in the morning and between 18:00 and 20:00 in the evening. These times allow the room to be arranged for activities in the middle of the day. Please close the freezer after each visit and keep bags away from the room's entrance. If an activity finishes late, the evening volunteer will still provide access during the stated period. Residents should contact that volunteer if the room appears locked when access should be available.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: If you no longer need your basket, tell the committee rather than lending it privately to another household. The committee can then offer the space to someone on the waiting list and update the contact record. Extra baskets may become available in the second week if demand falls, but residents should not plan around receiving one. If the renovation takes longer than expected, the committee will announce a revised end date and keep the existing basket bookings active. It will also ask whether any households need to change their arrangements. A delay will not automatically cancel your confirmed place in the temporary freezer.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: When the renovated kitchen is ready, the committee will announce a return period at least two days in advance. Residents should check that their labels are still readable before moving containers back. Borrowed boxes should be returned empty and clean after the transfer. The temporary freezer will remain in the meeting room until the committee has contacted every household with a confirmed basket. Please report practical problems through the committee's usual message address, including your basket number when relevant. The aim is to make limited space manageable through clear information, while avoiding repeated visits to the meeting room to find out what is happening.

title: Migration proposal: giving deleted records a recovery period
summary: Nhóm đề xuất thời hạn khôi phục cho hồ sơ bị xóa trong công cụ nội bộ. Kế hoạch phân biệt hồ sơ đang hoạt động và đã xóa, giữ nguyên quyền truy cập và kiểm tra trước khi triển khai rộng.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The internal equipment tracker currently removes a record as soon as a user confirms deletion. Last month, a coordinator deleted a projector record while trying to remove an empty draft with a similar name. The team recovered the information from an earlier backup, but the recovery required an engineer and did not include the coordinator's most recent note. The product team now proposes a fourteen-day recovery period for ordinary deletions. During that period, a deleted record would disappear from active lists but remain available in a separate recovery area. The proposal concerns equipment records only; it does not change how uploaded documents are managed.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The proposed change would add a deletion date and the identity of the person who deleted each record. Active lists would show records without a deletion date. The recovery area would show deleted records that were still within the recovery period. This sounds like a small change, but several screens currently obtain their lists in different ways. A forgotten screen might continue showing a deleted projector as available for booking. Before implementation, the team will list every place where equipment records appear, including exports and weekly summaries. Each place needs an explicit decision about whether deleted records belong in its results.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Recovery should preserve the record's identity, including its existing equipment number and history. However, restoring an item should not automatically make it available for a new booking. Someone may have deleted it because it was being removed from service, rather than by mistake. A restored record will therefore return with the status awaiting review. An authorised coordinator must check its condition information and current location before marking it available again. The recovery screen will explain this extra step beside the restore button. This makes restoration slightly slower, but it avoids treating every recovered record as equipment that can immediately be used.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The team considered allowing anyone who could view equipment to restore a record. That would make recovery convenient, especially when the original coordinator was absent. However, viewing rights do not currently include permission to change equipment details. The proposal therefore keeps recovery within the existing editing permissions. Users who can only view records may send a recovery request to a coordinator. The request will include the equipment number and the reason for restoration. Deleting a record will not remove its access restrictions, and the recovery area will apply the same restrictions. This prevents the recovery feature from becoming an unexpected route to previously hidden information.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: At the end of fourteen days, a scheduled process will remove the record from the recovery area. The interface will show the remaining recovery time before that point, so users do not have to calculate it from a date. The team does not plan to extend the period each time someone opens the record. Otherwise, frequently viewed records could remain recoverable indefinitely. Coordinators who need equipment history for ongoing work should keep the record active and change its operational status instead of deleting it. The help text will distinguish these choices with examples, because a recovery feature should not replace a clear record-management process.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Existing active records will receive no deletion date when the change is introduced. Records that were already permanently removed will not reappear. The first trial will involve the facilities team, which manages a small but varied equipment list. Testing will cover deletion, restoration, restricted access, and removal after the recovery period. It will also check that active exports exclude deleted records and that a restored record keeps its original number. During the trial, an engineer will compare the active list with the recovery area each day. Any item appearing in both places will be investigated before the feature is offered to another team.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The proposal accepts extra storage and a more complicated set of list rules in exchange for easier recovery from ordinary mistakes. Facilities staff support the change, but they have asked for clear responsibility when a recovered item awaits review. The coordinator who restores it will become the contact for that review unless another person accepts the task. After two weeks of trial use, the team will examine recovery requests, questions from users, and any unexpected list behaviour. Approval for wider use will depend on those findings. The intended result is a useful second chance, with visible limits and no automatic return to service.

title: Auction handover: offering retired office equipment to staff
summary: Công ty tổ chức bán nội bộ một số thiết bị văn phòng đã ngừng sử dụng. Bản bàn giao quy định cách mô tả tình trạng, xem hàng, đặt giá và nhận đồ, đồng thời xử lý những trường hợp cần rút món hàng khỏi danh sách.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: After the office renovation, the facilities team identified several desks, lamps, and monitor stands that the company no longer needed. Some were in good condition, while others had visible marks or missing accessories. Rather than arrange immediate collection by a recycling service, the office manager approved a small internal auction for staff. This handover explains how the auction should run while the manager is away next week. Only items on the approved list may be offered. Equipment still assigned to a department must remain outside the auction, even if it happens to be stored beside the retired items in the loading area.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Before publishing the list, Mei will check each item against its description and photograph. The description should include dimensions, visible damage, and any missing part that affects ordinary use. A photograph alone is not enough, because a desk may look attractive from the front while having a damaged drawer behind it. Mei should avoid broad claims such as perfect condition unless the inspection supports them. Items whose condition cannot be described clearly should be set aside for the office manager's return. The auction is intended to move useful surplus equipment, but that aim does not justify guessing about what a buyer will receive.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Staff may inspect the items on Tuesday between 12:00 and 14:00. The inspection will take place in the loading area, with the clear walking route marked before visitors arrive. Anyone interested in a desk should check its size against the space at home rather than rely on how small it looks in a large room. Facilities staff can explain the recorded condition but will not suggest repair methods. People unable to attend may request an additional photograph or measurement by Monday afternoon. Mei will add any useful new information to the shared list so that all potential buyers receive the same details.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Bids must be submitted through the internal form by Wednesday at 17:00. Each entry should identify the item number, the amount offered, and the employee's collection plan. A person may bid on several items but should consider whether they could collect all of them if successful. The highest valid bid will receive the first offer. If two bids are equal, the earlier submitted bid will take priority. Mei will not share individual bid amounts while the auction is open, since that could give later bidders information that earlier bidders did not have. A submitted bid can be withdrawn before the closing time.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Successful bidders will receive a message on Thursday morning and must reply by the end of that day. Payment instructions will be included in that message, and the facilities team will check the payment record before releasing an item. If the first bidder declines or does not reply, Mei may contact the next person on the bid list. She should record the reason for moving to that person so that the result remains understandable. Staff who were not successful will receive a short closing notice. Items without a buyer will stay in the loading area until the manager decides on the next arrangement.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Collection will take place on Friday afternoon by appointment. Buyers must arrange suitable transport and enough help to move their items; the company will not provide a delivery service. Large desks will remain assembled for collection because the facilities team has not checked whether repeated assembly would affect their condition. The appointment message will repeat the item's measurements and identify the entrance to use. Buyers should not arrive through reception with a vehicle intended for the loading area. If transport falls through, they must contact Mei before their appointment. She can consider another available slot, but cannot promise storage beyond the following Monday.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: If an item is damaged or a description proves inaccurate before collection, Mei should pause its sale and contact the successful bidder. The buyer should receive the updated information before deciding whether to continue. An item needed again by the company must also be withdrawn, with a clear explanation to everyone who bid on it. At the end of the week, Mei will prepare a summary showing items sold, items withdrawn, payments confirmed, and collections completed. The office manager will use that summary to decide whether another auction would be worthwhile. The measure of success is an orderly transfer, not simply an empty loading area.

title: Repair estimate: bringing a mechanical wall clock back into use
summary: Chủ cửa hàng giải thích các lựa chọn sửa đồng hồ treo tường cơ cũ. Khách hàng cân nhắc giữ bộ máy nguyên bản, thời gian thử sau sửa và giới hạn của việc làm mới vỏ ngoài.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Thank you for bringing your wall clock to our workshop on Saturday. You explained that it had belonged to your grandparents and had recently begun stopping after a few hours. You also said that keeping its original character mattered more to you than making the case look new. We have completed the initial inspection and prepared this estimate before starting any repair. The clock is still at the workshop, and no parts have been replaced. This document separates the work needed to investigate the stopping problem from optional work on the wooden case, so you can decide which result would suit your plans.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: During the inspection, the clock ran for just over three hours before stopping. We found old deposits around several moving parts, but a full examination will require removing the mechanism from the case. The first option is a service of the original mechanism, estimated at 1,200,000 dong if no replacement parts are needed. This includes cleaning, reassembly, and a period of observation at the workshop. It does not include repairing damage that only becomes visible after the mechanism is opened. If we find such damage, we will send photographs and a revised estimate before continuing beyond the work you have approved.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The main uncertainty concerns a small part that controls the movement of the hands. It appears worn, but we cannot judge the extent of that wear while it remains in place. If it needs replacement, a suitable part may have to be ordered from a specialist supplier. We would not place that order without your agreement. An ordered part could add both cost and waiting time, especially if the supplier needs measurements before confirming availability. You may choose to stop the repair at that stage and collect the clock after paying for the inspection and any service work already completed.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A second option would replace the original mechanism with a battery-powered unit while keeping the visible face and wooden case. That option is estimated at 850,000 dong, but it would change how the clock operates and remove its original winding routine. Because you mentioned the clock's family history, we are presenting this as a separate choice rather than treating it as the default repair. If you select it, we will return the original mechanism to you in a labelled box. Keeping that mechanism would allow you to discuss a different restoration later, although we cannot promise what a future workshop might be able to do.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The wooden case has scratches and one loose decorative strip near the bottom. Securing the strip would cost an additional 150,000 dong. Refinishing the whole case would require a separate estimate after you choose the colour and finish you want. We do not recommend deciding from a photograph alone, because the room's light can change how a sample looks. You can visit the workshop to compare samples beside the clock. If preserving the familiar appearance is your priority, you may prefer to secure the loose strip and leave the scratches. Cosmetic work will not be included unless you specifically request it.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: After servicing the original mechanism, we would observe the clock for seven days before inviting you to collect it. This period would help us identify another early stop under workshop conditions. It would not guarantee identical behaviour in every home setting. At collection, we would show you how we positioned the clock during observation and discuss any instructions relevant to the completed work. If a new part has been ordered, the seven-day observation would begin after that part is fitted. For this reason, a supplier's delivery date should not be understood as the date when the whole repair will be ready.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Please reply with the option you prefer and whether you want the decorative strip secured. If you would like to discuss the choices in person, we can keep the clock here until next Friday without starting work. After that, please arrange either approval or collection so that we can manage workshop space. Our written confirmation will list the agreed work, estimated charge, and any condition requiring a further decision. We understand that this clock has personal value beyond its usefulness. A clear agreement now will help us preserve what matters to you while keeping unexpected costs and changes visible throughout the repair.

title: Release plan: separating personal bookmarks from team shortcuts
summary: Ứng dụng bổ sung lối tắt chung cho nhóm nhưng giữ dấu trang cá nhân độc lập. Kế hoạch làm rõ quyền quản lý, cách chuyển lối tắt sang khu vực chung và xử lý liên kết không còn truy cập được.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The project workspace currently offers one list of bookmarks for each user. People use it to reach frequently visited pages, such as a project schedule or a supplier discussion. Team leaders have asked for shared shortcuts so that new colleagues can find important pages without requesting a list in chat. The proposed release will add a team shortcut section beside the existing personal bookmarks. It will not combine the two lists. This distinction matters because a useful team starting point is different from an individual's daily working route. Someone may need a private bookmark to an unfinished task without making that task prominent for everyone.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Team shortcuts will be managed by users who already have permission to edit the team's workspace settings. Ordinary team members will be able to open them but will not change their titles or destinations. The team considered allowing every member to edit the list, which could make maintenance faster. However, customers in the planning interviews wanted a stable starting point, especially during a busy project. They preferred to send suggestions to an owner rather than discover that a familiar shortcut had changed overnight. Each shortcut will therefore show a contact name, giving users a clear route for reporting an outdated or confusing entry.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Existing personal bookmarks will remain in their current order when the feature arrives. Nothing will become a team shortcut automatically. A workspace owner may create a shared shortcut from an existing bookmark, but the interface will first ask for a team title and a short description of its purpose. The owner's personal copy will remain unchanged. This avoids a situation in which preparing a useful team list unexpectedly rearranges someone's private workspace. Owners will also be able to create a shortcut by entering a destination directly. The first version will accept pages inside the workspace, while links to external websites will remain personal bookmarks.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A shared shortcut will not grant access to its destination. If a page is restricted, a member without access will see an explanation rather than the page's contents. During shortcut creation, the owner will receive a warning when the destination is not available to every team member. The owner can choose another page or keep the shortcut with a description explaining who can use it. Some teams have legitimate reasons for a shortcut used only by a smaller working group. The product team therefore chose a visible warning over a complete ban, while keeping the underlying access rules unchanged.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The list will have a limit of eight team shortcuts in the first release. Interview participants said that a long menu of important links often stopped being useful because almost everything was described as important. Owners will need to choose destinations that help people begin common work, rather than include every project document. They can reorder the shortcuts, and the same order will appear for all team members. Personal bookmarks will still allow individuals to keep their preferred working sequence. The help example will show a short shared list containing a project overview, an agreed schedule, and a page explaining where to ask questions.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Before release, testing will cover creating, renaming, reordering, and removing a shared shortcut. It will also include destinations that are deleted, moved, or restricted after the shortcut was created. An unavailable destination should leave the shortcut visible with an explanation, so that users can report the problem instead of wondering where an entry went. The trial will involve three teams with different working patterns, including one that changes project pages frequently. Support will collect questions about the difference between the two lists. If several people assume that deleting a shared shortcut deletes the destination page, the wording will need revision before wider release.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Workspace owners will receive the feature announcement before ordinary members, allowing them to prepare a small useful list. The announcement will include the ownership rules, access warning, and eight-shortcut limit. For the first week, the team shortcut section will include a short explanation of how it differs from personal bookmarks. After the trial, the product team will review whether members can find common pages more easily and whether owners can maintain the list without frequent support requests. The team has postponed requests for coloured icons and usage rankings. Clear purpose and predictable behaviour are the priorities for this version of the feature.

title: Invoice procedure: correcting a supplier document without losing its history
summary: Quy trình nội bộ hướng dẫn nhân viên xử lý hóa đơn nhà cung cấp có thông tin sai. Nhóm giữ bản gốc, xác minh thông tin với người nhận hàng, yêu cầu bản sửa và theo dõi tránh xử lý cả hai phiên bản.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: This procedure applies when a supplier sends a document that does not match the company's purchase record or confirmed delivery. Recent examples include an incorrect purchase number, a description for the wrong product size, and a delivery charge that was not included in the agreed quotation. These differences should be checked before the document enters the ordinary payment workflow. The procedure describes our internal handling and communication; questions about the correct external document format should be referred to the finance team. Staff should not alter a supplier's document themselves, even when the mistake appears small and the correct information seems obvious from an email.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The first person who notices a difference should save the received document in the purchase folder and mark its status awaiting clarification. The original file must remain available throughout the check. A note should identify the field in question and the information it appears to conflict with. For example, a useful note would state that the document lists twenty large storage boxes while the receiving record shows twenty small boxes. A comment saying invoice wrong is too vague for a colleague to act on. The note should also include the supplier contact and the date when the difference was first reported internally.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before asking the supplier for a correction, the purchase owner should check the order, any approved changes, and the receiving record. A later agreement may explain a difference that initially looks like an error. If the quantity or product description is uncertain, the purchase owner should speak to the colleague who received the delivery. Finance staff cannot confirm what arrived merely by comparing two documents that may both contain the same mistake. For a delivery still in progress, the owner should record what has been confirmed and what remains unknown. The request to the supplier should distinguish established facts from questions that still need an answer.

A corrected product description does not prove that the quantity and charge are still the same. The original entry should be marked replaced, with a reference to the revised document. Only the version confirmed by finance should continue into the payment workflow. title: Library notice: borrowing board games with a clear return check
summary: Thư viện mở dịch vụ cho mượn trò chơi bàn. Thông báo hướng dẫn chọn trò, kiểm tra linh kiện, báo thiếu đồ và trả đúng nơi để người mượn tiếp theo không gặp bất ngờ.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: From next month, Oak Street Library will lend a small collection of board games as well as books. The collection includes short games for two people and longer games for groups, with information about playing time on each box. Library members may borrow one game at a time for ten days. The service is intended for people who want to try a game before deciding whether it suits their household. It is also useful for an occasional gathering when buying a new game would make little sense. Games will be kept behind the information desk rather than on the ordinary open shelves.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: A catalogue at the desk will show the number of players, suggested playing time, and language used in each game's instructions. These details should help members choose something that fits their plans. A long game requiring six players may not be suitable for a quiet evening with one neighbour. Some games contain printed English on the cards, while others rely mainly on pictures and numbers. Staff can show you a sample card before you borrow. They cannot promise that every member of your group will enjoy the same game, but they can help you understand what a game requires before taking it home.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Each box contains a printed inventory and several small bags for organising pieces. At checkout, a member of staff will open the box with you and compare its contents with the inventory. This check usually takes about five minutes, so please allow more time than you would for borrowing a book. If a piece is already missing, the record will state what is absent and whether the game can still be played as intended. You may choose a different game after hearing that information. Please keep the inventory inside the box, since it will also be used when the game returns.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: At home, choose a place where small pieces are easy to see and keep the game's bags together. Before packing the box, compare the contents with the inventory rather than relying on the box lid closing comfortably. If you discover that something is missing, contact the library and explain which piece you cannot find. Please do not buy a replacement or borrow a piece from another game without speaking to staff. Similar-looking pieces may serve different purposes. Staff will record your message and tell you how to return the remaining contents so that the next borrower receives accurate information.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Games must be returned to the information desk during staffed opening hours. Do not put them in the outside book-return box, where loose contents could become separated and the return could not be checked with you. A staff member will compare the pieces with the inventory and record any difference from the checkout note. If the desk is busy, you may leave the closed box with staff and provide a contact number for questions. The return will then be checked later that day. Keep your borrowing receipt until the library confirms that the return has been recorded on your account.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: You may request one extension if nobody else has reserved the game. Please make that request before the return date rather than assuming that the game is still available because you have heard nothing from the library. Reservations can be made through the desk or the library's usual online account page. A reservation means you will be contacted when the game is ready, not that it will arrive by the date of a particular party. If your gathering depends on a specific game, staff suggest making another plan as well. Returned games sometimes need an additional check before they can be lent again.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The library will review the service after three months. Members are invited to comment on the catalogue, the condition of the games, and the time needed for checkout and return. Suggestions for additional games are welcome, especially when they explain who might use them and what makes them different from the existing collection. Staff will also record which games are often requested but unavailable. A popular title may justify a second copy, although the library must balance that choice against offering more variety. Clear checks and honest information will help the collection remain useful as more households begin to use it.

title: Support investigation: a progress bar that finished before the import
summary: Thanh tiến độ của công cụ nhập dữ liệu đạt 100% khi tệp vừa truyền xong, dù việc kiểm tra và tạo bản ghi vẫn đang diễn ra. Nhóm xác minh dữ liệu không mất và thiết kế trạng thái theo từng giai đoạn.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: On Wednesday afternoon, a customer reported that a contact import had reached one hundred percent but the new contacts were not visible. She waited briefly, then refreshed the page and began the import again. Several minutes later, both attempts appeared in the import history, and she asked support whether the first attempt had failed. The support agent, Bao, could see that both jobs had completed, but the customer's account of the screen suggested a different problem. He asked for the file size, the approximate start time, and a description of the final message. The customer remembered a full progress bar but no completion message.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Bao reproduced the behaviour using a sample file with invented names and email addresses. The bar reached one hundred percent as soon as the file finished travelling from the browser to the service. The import then continued through validation and record creation, but the screen did not explain those stages. For a small file, this gap was barely noticeable. With a larger file, Bao saw a full bar remain on screen for more than a minute while the contacts were still unavailable. The customer had reasonably interpreted the full bar as the end of the entire operation, although it measured only the transfer.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The engineer who joined the investigation confirmed that the records were not being lost. The first attempt had continued after the customer refreshed the page because the service had already received the file and created an import job. However, the browser did not reconnect to that job when the customer returned. It offered the starting screen again, making a second attempt look like the natural next step. The import history contained the information needed to understand the first attempt, but that history was on another page. Support therefore had to explain both the misleading bar and the missing route back to the active job.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: As an immediate measure, support added a notice beside the upload control stating that file transfer was followed by processing. It also directed users to import history before starting again after a refresh. The team avoided telling users that every long wait was normal, since an import could still encounter a genuine problem. Bao's reply explained what had happened in this particular case and identified the two completed jobs by their start times. He did not ask the customer to repeat the import for testing. The engineering team already had a sample file that reproduced the confusing behaviour without using her contact information.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The proposed interface change would separate three stages: transferring the file, checking its contents, and creating records. Only the transfer stage would use a percentage, because the current service could measure that stage directly. During the other stages, the interface would show the current activity and the job's start time. The team rejected an animated percentage that advanced according to a fixed timer. It might look reassuring, but it would still suggest knowledge about remaining work that the application did not possess. The final screen would report the number of records created and provide a separate explanation for any rows that were not accepted.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: A second change would reconnect the browser to the latest active import after a refresh. Users would see that work was continuing and could open its details without submitting the file again. The team would also show a warning before starting another import while one was active, although it would not prohibit the action. Some customers intentionally import separate files close together, so a complete block would interfere with legitimate work. Testing would include a refresh during each stage, an unsuccessful job, and two deliberate imports. The engineers would check the displayed job number as well as the message, since correct wording attached to the wrong job would remain misleading.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Support and engineering agreed to trial the changes with customers who regularly imported larger files. They would compare questions about apparently finished imports before and after the trial, while checking whether the new warning interrupted valid repeated work. Bao would review the messages to ensure that they described observable activity rather than promising an exact finishing time. The team also planned to update the help page with a screenshot of each stage. The investigation showed that a technically accurate measurement can create a false overall impression when its scope is unclear. The release would aim to make the whole process understandable, including what continues after the transfer ends.
